claim: For user systemd services to start at boot without login on a headless system, lingering must be enabled first: loginctl enable-linger <user>
stance_target: lingering is the prerequisite for headless user-service deployment of an agent
scope_conditions: headless Linux with systemd; user-scoped services
quoted_support: First and foremost, for systemd services associated with a specific user to start at boot time (without requiring the user to log in), we need to enable systemd user lingering. This feature allows user-specific services to persist beyond user sessions, which is exactly what we need in a headless setup.

claim: On Debian-based systems the dbus-user-session package automatically configures the user/session bus wiring needed for systemd user services; on other distros the dbus.socket (ListenStream=%t/bus, ExecStartPost sets DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=%t/bus) and dbus.service (dbus-daemon --session --address=systemd: --systemd-activation, Requires=dbus.socket) user units must be created manually under /usr/lib/systemd/user
stance_target: on systemd-era hosts the user bus is socket-activated at /run/user/<uid>/bus rather than per-login dbus-launch
scope_conditions: Debian for the package path; non-Debian for the manual unit files; systemd user services
quoted_support: As Debian system users, this package automatically configures most of what's needed for DBus user sessions. ... ListenStream=%t/bus – specifies the path of the socket, with %t replaced with the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR ... ExecStartPost – sets the DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS environment variable, ensuring subsequent services can locate the session bus

claim: User services that consume the session bus should declare Requires=dbus.socket, and services exposing a D-Bus name can use Type=dbus with BusName=<name> so systemd activates them on the session bus
stance_target: an agent that talks D-Bus as a user service should order itself against dbus.socket
scope_conditions: systemd user services using the session bus
quoted_support: Requires=dbus.socket – ensures that the dbus.socket starts before this DBus service ... [Service] Type=dbus BusName=com.example.mydbusserver ExecStart=/path/to/server/executable

claim: The bashrc/profile pattern 'eval $(dbus-launch --sh-syntax --exit-with-session)' that Baeldung recommends for non-systemd environments conflicts with the systemd-managed shared user bus and is the anti-pattern to avoid on NixOS, where the user bus already exists at /run/user/<uid>/bus
stance_target: reliance on dbus-launch shell-profile automation as a headless-agent bus solution on modern systemd hosts
evidence_type: expert-opinion (tutorial, reviewed) — cross-checked against Chimera docs and Arch forum thread which explicitly warn against dbus-launch/dbus-run-session on user-bus systems
scope_conditions: systemd hosts with user services (e.g. NixOS); only valid on non-systemd distros
quoted_support: if test -z "$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS"; then # Only start D-Bus if it's not already running eval `dbus-launch --sh-syntax --exit-with-session` fi

claim: systemd resource controls (e.g. MemoryLimit=100M) and journald logging via journalctl -u are the recommended practices for headless services that cannot be observed directly
stance_target: headless fleet agents should carry systemd resource limits and journald logging by default
quoted_support: we can use systemd's resource control features to limit the amount of CPU, memory, and other resources that these services can use. For instance, to limit memory usage ... add a memory limit to our service file ... MemoryLimit=100M
